#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-timeout-applies-test.sh
#
# SPEC-1 (#1801): A hung work unit dispatched through the fanout, map, or
# sequential strategy stops at its stage template `timeout_s:` limit; the
# 300 s flat deadline no longer applies.
#
# Old code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"
# New code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
#
# This test fails on old code (spy captures 300), passes on new code
# (spy captures the template's timeout_s: value).
#
# [#1801/SPEC-1]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# template.sh also sources scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

print_test_header "orch strategies pass template timeout_s: (not 300s) to orch_collect (#1801 SPEC-1)"
setup_test_env "orch-timeout-applies"

# ── Template with timeout_s: 7 for stage "testjob" ──────────────────────────
# The spy test asserts orch_collect receives --timeout 7, NOT --timeout 300.
TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tpl-spec1.yaml"
cat > "$TPL" <<'YAML'
id: tpl-spec1
name: spec1 test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
flow:
  - testjob
testjob:
  roles: [testworker]
  timeout_s: 7
YAML
load_template "$TPL" >/dev/null 2>&1

# Source the strategies (after template.sh so _TPL_SOURCE_FILE is set)
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"

# ── Minimal plugin for resolve_plugin_for_role ───────────────────────────────
_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/testworker"
mkdir -p "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: testworker
name: testworker
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: testworker_run
provides:
  role: testworker
MF
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" <<'PL'
testworker_run() { return 0; }
PL

# Mock orch functions, platform detection, and plugin resolution so the
# strategy machinery runs without a real backend or runner environment.
_DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")
resolve_plugin_for_role() { printf '%s\n' "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"; return 0; }

_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_SPEC1_OC_CALLS=0
orch_collect() {
    _SPEC1_OC_CALLS=$(( _SPEC1_OC_CALLS + 1 ))
    _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
    local _s1_pool="$1"; shift
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --timeout) _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
            *) shift ;;
        esac
    done
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
    return 0
}
orch_spawn()    { return 0; }
orch_dispatch() { printf 'slot-%s\n' "$$"; return 0; }
orch_shutdown() { return 0; }

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
printf '{"schema_version":1}' > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
export ZBUILD_RUN_ID="spec1-test"
export ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-scratch"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"
export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="testjob"

_spec1_expected_timeout="$(template_stage_time_limit testjob)"

# ── SPEC-1a: fanout passes template timeout_s: (not 300) to orch_collect ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect"
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1a_rc=0
_strategy_run_fanout "pool-fanout-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi

# With ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 set explicitly, new code must still ignore it
export ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1a2_rc=0
_strategy_run_fanout "pool-fanout-spec1b" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a2_rc=$?
if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 does not override template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout}) must win over ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300" \
        "spy got --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true

# ── SPEC-1b: sequential passes template timeout_s: (not 300) to orch_collect ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect"
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1b_rc=0
_strategy_run_sequential "pool-seq-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1b_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi

# With ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 set, sequential must still use template value
export ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1b2_rc=0
_strategy_run_sequential "pool-seq-spec1b" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1b2_rc=$?
if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 does not override template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout}) must win over ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300" \
        "spy got --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'"
fi
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true

# ── SPEC-1c: map strategy static guard — no longer references ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT ─
# map strategy is too complex to spy on (FIFO pool, sub-pools, batch dispatch),
# but the static guard catches the pattern change at source level.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy no longer uses ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (static guard)"
_MAP_SH="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0: map.sh exists" "$_MAP_SH"
if grep -q 'template_stage_time_limit' "$_MAP_SH"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy calls template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect timeout"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy must call template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect timeout" \
        "not found in $_MAP_SH; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300"
fi
if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_MAP_SH"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy does not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (flat 300 s deadline removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy must not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (flat 300 s deadline)" \
        "ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still present in $_MAP_SH"
fi

# ── SPEC-1d: fanout and sequential also have no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT reference ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout and sequential source files have no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT"
for _s1_strat in fanout sequential; do
    _s1_file="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/${_s1_strat}.sh"
    if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_s1_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] ${_s1_strat}.sh: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT removed (flat 300 s deadline gone)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] ${_s1_strat}.sh: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT must not remain" \
            "still present in $_s1_file; the 300 s flat deadline applies on old code"
    fi
done

# ── SPEC-1 (map runtime spy): map passes template timeout_s: to orch_collect ──
# map.sh uses ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 on old code; must use template_stage_time_limit
# on new code. The spy (defined above) is still the capturing version at this point.
# Fails on old code (spy captures 300); passes on new code (spy captures _spec1_expected_timeout).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect (runtime spy)"
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1m_rc=0
_strategy_run_map "pool-map-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1m_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi

# With ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 explicitly set, map must still ignore it.
export ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1m2_rc=0
_strategy_run_map "pool-map-spec1b" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1m2_rc=$?
if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 does not override template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout}) must win over ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300" \
        "spy got --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true

# ── SPEC-1e: _orch_local_collect_results sets _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=timed_out ─
# This is a runtime test: start a real hung process, run collect with a 2 s
# timeout, and assert the outcome variable is "timed_out" not "failed".
# Fails on old code (sets "failed" because rc=124 is just a non-zero exit).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] _orch_local_collect_results sets timed_out outcome on timeout"
# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/local_engine.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
# proc-group.sh must be available so the new kill path compiles cleanly.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/proc-group.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"

_s1e_pool="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec1e-pool"
mkdir -p "$_s1e_pool/pids" "$_s1e_pool/results"

# Start a process that will run for 60 s — it will never write a .exit file.
sleep 60 &
_s1e_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$_s1e_pid" > "$_s1e_pool/pids/spec1e.pid"

_s1e_rc=0
_orch_local_collect_results "$_s1e_pool" "pids" 2 || _s1e_rc=$?
_s1e_outcome="$_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME"

# Ensure the sleeping process is cleaned up regardless of outcome.
kill "$_s1e_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_s1e_pid" 2>/dev/null || true

if [[ "$_s1e_outcome" == "timed_out" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] _orch_local_collect_results sets _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=timed_out on timeout"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] _orch_local_collect_results must set _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=timed_out on timeout" \
        "got '${_s1e_outcome:-<empty>}'; old code sets 'failed' because rc=124 counts as a non-zero exit"
fi

# ── SPEC-1f: strategy propagates timed_out outcome; output names stage+limit ─
# Mock orch_collect to simulate a timeout (return 1 with _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=
# "timed_out"). Assert the strategy (a) propagates _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
# and (b) emits the stage name and the limit to stderr.
# Fails on old code: old code has no timed_out branch → _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
# and no stage/limit in the timeout message.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] strategy propagates timed_out; output names stage and limit exceeded"
orch_collect() {
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"
    return 1
}

_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=""
_s1f_timeout="$(template_stage_time_limit testjob)"
# Run directly in the parent shell (not a subshell) so _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME
# set inside _strategy_run_fanout is visible after the call. Capture all output
# (stdout + stderr) to a temp file and read it back into _s1f_stderr.
_s1f_stderr_file="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec1f-stderr.txt"
_s1f_rc=0
_strategy_run_fanout "pool-spec1f" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" >"$_s1f_stderr_file" 2>&1 || _s1f_rc=$?

if [[ "${_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: the orch-sequential plugin is removed from the installed tree (#1801,
# SPEC-3). A guard that passes while the directory still exists would let a
# trivially-present plugin defeat the whole point of SPEC-2's no-fallback rule.
#
# Two assertions:
#   1. The plugin directory itself does not exist in the installed tree.
#   2. No code or config file outside docs/adr/ still names "orch-sequential"
#      (the golden file, manifests, contract.sh hardcoded path, test references).
#
# Both must FAIL on current code (the directory exists and is referenced
# throughout) and PASS after the implementation removes the plugin.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-3]
set -uo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch-sequential is absent from the installed tree (#1801 SPEC-3)"
setup_test_env "orch-sequential-absent-guard"

# ── SPEC-3a: plugin directory does not exist ─────────────────────────────────
_orch_seq_dir="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential"
if [[ ! -d "$_orch_seq_dir" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] orch-sequential plugin directory does not exist"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] orch-sequential plugin directory does not exist" \
        "directory still present: $_orch_seq_dir"
fi

# ── SPEC-3b: no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential ──
# Files allowed to reference orch-sequential: docs/adr/ (ADR prose)
# Files NOT allowed: core/, plugins/, scripts/, config/, tests/, .github/
_hits=""
while IFS= read -r _f; do
    # Skip docs/adr/ — ADR prose is allowed to name the deleted plugin
    case "$_f" in
        */docs/adr/*) continue ;;
        # Skip the guard test itself (this file)
        */orch-sequential-absent-guard-test.sh) continue ;;
    esac
    _hits="${_hits}${_f}"$'\n'
done < <(grep -rl "orch-sequential" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/core" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/config" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/tests" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/.github" \
    2>/dev/null || true)

# Remove trailing newline for display
_hits="${_hits%$'\n'}"
if [[ -z "$_hits" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] no code or config file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential" \
        "still referenced in: $(printf '%s' "$_hits" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

print_test_results

# A8: within the form's `id: adr` entry (up to the next `- type:`), `required: true`.

assert_eq "[A8] the issue form requires the ADR § field" "yes" "$_a8"

# ── SPEC-7 (#1801): ADR-011 and ADR-017 have Enforced by sections, not in baseline
# Verifies: (a) each ADR file carries an `## Enforced by` section, and
#           (b) neither file appears in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt.
# "must pass after this change; it need not fail before."
ADR_011="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md"
ADR_017="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-017-per-stage-router-config.md"

if grep -q '## Enforced by' "$ADR_011" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-011 carries an ## Enforced by section"
else

if grep -q '## Enforced by' "$ADR_017" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-017 carries an ## Enforced by section"
else

if ! grep -q 'ADR-011' "$BASELINE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-011.md is not in the enforcement baseline (it has its section)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-011.md must be removed from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
        "ADR-011 still listed in $BASELINE; remove the entry once the ## Enforced by section is added"
fi
if ! grep -q 'ADR-017' "$BASELINE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-017.md is not in the enforcement baseline (it has its section)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] ADR-017.md must be removed from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
        "ADR-017 still listed in $BASELINE; remove the entry once the ## Enforced by section is added"
fi

_reset; _adr ADR-908-x "Accepted" 'Covered by the unit tests, see the suite.'; _lint

assert_contains "[A9] it says the section names no test" "$out" "names no test"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
18	# the process group would.
19	#
20	# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
21	# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
26	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
27	
28	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
29	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
30	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
32	
33	print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
34	setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
35	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
36	
37	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
38	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
39	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
40	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
41	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
42	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"
43	
44	# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
45	# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
46	# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
47	# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
48	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
49	ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
50	mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
51	cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
52	
53	mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
54	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
55	mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null
56	
57	# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
58	# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
59	# no-op rather than a witness.
60	# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
61	# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
62	# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
63	# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
64	for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
65	    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
66	    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
67	    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
68	id: $_id
69	name: Test $_id
70	kind: $_kind
71	version: 0.0.1
72	hooks:
73	  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
74	  cleanup: $_fn
75	requires:
76	  core:
77	    - redaction
78	provides:
79	  result_contract: 3
80	outputs:
81	  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
82	    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
83	    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
84	    format: json
85	    required: true
86	    primary: true
87	EOF
88	done
89	
90	# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
91	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
92	intake_run() {
93	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
94	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
95	    return 0
96	}
97	intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
98	PLUG
99	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
100	build_run() {
101	    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
102	    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
103	        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
104	    fi
105	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
106	    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
107	    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
108	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
109	    else
110	        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
111	    fi
112	    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
113	}
114	build_cleanup() {
115	    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
116	    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
117	    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
118	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
119	        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
120	        sleep 120
121	    fi
122	    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
123	        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
124	        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
125	        wait
126	    fi
127	    return 0
128	}
129	PLUG
130	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
131	test_run() {
132	    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
133	    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
134	    return 0
135	}
136	test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
137	PLUG

139	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
140	install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
141	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
142	mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
143	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
144	
145	_case_no=0
146	# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
147	_prep() {
148	    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
149	    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
150	    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
151	    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
152	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
153	    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
154	    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
155	    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
156	    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
157	    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
158	}
159	
160	# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
161	#
162	# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
163	# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
164	# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
165	# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
166	# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
167	# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
168	#
169	# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
170	# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
171	#
172	# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
173	# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
174	# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
175	# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
176	# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
177	# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
178	# returns, which a killed stage never does.
179	_assert_released() {
180	    local _case="$1"; shift
181	    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
182	    local _stage _missing=""
183	    for _stage in "$@"; do
184	        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
185	    done
186	    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
187	        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
188	    else
189	        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
190	            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
191	    fi
192	    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
193	        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
194	    else
195	        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
196	    fi
197	}
198	
199	# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
200	# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
201	# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
202	# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
203	# are made below, in order.
204	#
205	# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
206	# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
207	# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
208	# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
209	_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
210	    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
211	    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
212	    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
213	    (
214	        _prep "$1"
215	        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
216	        _t0=$(date +%s)
217	        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
218	            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
219	        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
220	    ) &
221	}
222	_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!

228	# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
229	# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).

231	install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
232	if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
233	   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
234	    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"

236	cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'

238	extends: resume-minimal
239	release:
240	  timeout_s: 5
241	YAML
242	_start_blocking spec5-bound BLOCK_CLEANUP resume-spec5-bound; _SPEC5_BOUND_PID=$!
243	_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-spec5-bound"

245	# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
246	print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
247	_prep success
248	export BUILD_RC=0
249	set +e
250	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
251	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
252	_rc=$?
253	set -e
254	# SPEC-6/6b run alongside this case; if it fails, say what the runner said.
255	[[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] || tail -20 "$CASE_DIR/out" >&2
256	assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
257	_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test
258	
259	# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
260	print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
261	_prep nonzero
262	export BUILD_RC=1
263	set +e
264	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
265	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
266	_rc=$?
267	set -e
268	if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
269	    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
270	else
271	    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
272	fi

275	# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
276	print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
277	_prep sigint
278	export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
279	set +e
280	( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
281	    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
282	_rc=$?
283	set -e
284	# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
285	# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
286	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
287	assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \

289	_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

291	# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
292	print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
293	_prep sigterm
294	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
295	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
296	    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
297	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
298	    RUNNER_PID=$!
299	else
300	    set -m
301	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
302	        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
303	    RUNNER_PID=$!
304	    set +m
305	fi
306	for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
307	_build_pid="$(head -n 1 "$BUILD_STARTED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
308	_t0=$(date +%s)
309	kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
310	wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
311	_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
312	# ADR-054 §7: the runner acts on the signal while the stage is still running.
313	# Build holds for 30s; a runner that waits for it to return took 30s+ here.
314	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 15 ]]; then
315	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage (${_elapsed}s)"
316	else
317	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage" "took ${_elapsed}s; build holds 30s"
318	fi
319	if [[ -n "$_build_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
320	    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run" "build pid $_build_pid still alive"
321	    kill -KILL "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
322	else
323	    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run"
324	fi
325	# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
326	# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
327	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
328	_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build

330	# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
331	# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
332	#
333	# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
334	# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
335	# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
336	# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
337	# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
338	# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
339	# runs could never reproduce.
340	#
341	# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
342	# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
343	# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
344	# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
345	# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
346	print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
347	_prep timeout
348	export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
349	_tbin=""
350	if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
351	elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
352	fi
353	if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
354	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
355	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
356	else
357	    # [#1801/SPEC-5]: #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own
358	    # teardown budget, not guessed.
359	    #
360	    # After #1801 the engine bounds each always-run stage by template_stage_time_limit
361	    # (top-level `timeout_s:` in the stage block), NOT by router.timeout_s or
362	    # ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT. The template below pins timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT
363	    # for release so the worst case is knowable and the grace derives from it.
364	    # This case relies on its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound —
365	    # the grace is purely a safety net so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the
366	    # suite. Three stages release on this path, so an unpinned run could spend far
367	    # longer tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here.
368	    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
369	    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
370	    # Create a repo with a template that has timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT for
371	    # release (top-level, read by template_stage_time_limit after #1801).
372	    _spec5_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5")"
373	    install_template_overlay "$_spec5_repo" resume-minimal
374	    if [[ -d "$_spec5_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
375	       ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
376	        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude"
377	    fi
378	    cat > "$_spec5_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-timeout-bounded.yaml" <<YAMLEOF
379	id: resume-timeout-bounded
380	extends: resume-minimal
381	release:
382	  timeout_s: ${_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT}
383	YAMLEOF
384	    set -m
385	    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-timeout-bounded --goal "$3"' \
386	        _ "$_spec5_repo" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
387	    RUNNER_PID=$!
388	    set +m
389	    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
390	    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
391	    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
392	    _spec5_killer=$!
393	    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
394	    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
395	    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
396	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
397	    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
398	fi
399	
400	# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
401	# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
402	# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
403	# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
404	print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
405	wait "$_SPEC6_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
406	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6_DIR"
407	_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
408	# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
409	# `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block (read by template_stage_time_limit
410	# after #1801 — 30s in simple.yaml), so the runner returns in about 30s.
411	# Allow generous headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
412	if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
413	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
414	else
415	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
416	fi
417	# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
418	# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
419	# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
420	# runner returns; up to 1s covers the killed processes exiting on a loaded host.
421	_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
422	if [[ -n "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
423	    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
424	fi
425	if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
426	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
427	elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
428	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
429	    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
430	    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
431	    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
432	    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
433	    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
434	else
435	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
436	fi
437	
438	# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
439	# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
440	# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
441	# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
442	print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
443	# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
444	# case is only about what survives it.
445	wait "$_SPEC6B_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
446	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6B_DIR"
447	_child_pid=""
448	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
449	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
450	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
451	done
452	_alive=1
453	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
454	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
455	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
456	fi
457	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
458	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
459	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
460	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
461	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
462	else
463	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
464	fi
465	
466	# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
467	# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
468	# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
469	# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
470	# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
471	# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
472	# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
473	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
474	wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
475	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
476	_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
477	if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
478	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
479	else
480	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
481	        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
482	fi
483	
484	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
485	# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
486	# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
487	# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
488	if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
489	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
490	else
491	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
492	        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
493	fi
494	
495	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
496	# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
497	# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
498	# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
499	# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
500	# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
501	if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
502	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
503	else
504	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
505	        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
506	fi
507	
508	cleanup_test_env
509	print_test_results
510	exit $((FAIL > 0))
511

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#
# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
    (
        _prep "$1"
        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
        _t0=$(date +%s)
        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
    ) &
}
_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!
_start_blocking blocking-ignore-term BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM; _SPEC6B_PID=$!
_SPEC6_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking"
_SPEC6B_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking-ignore-term"

# [#1801/SPEC-5]: blocking run with timeout_s: 5 for release (top-level, read
# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).
_spec5_bound_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5-bound")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: resume-spec5-bound
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: 5
YAML
_start_blocking spec5-bound BLOCK_CLEANUP resume-spec5-bound; _SPEC5_BOUND_PID=$!
_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-spec5-bound"

# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
_prep success
export BUILD_RC=0
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# SPEC-6/6b run alongside this case; if it fails, say what the runner said.
[[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] || tail -20 "$CASE_DIR/out" >&2
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test

# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
_prep nonzero
export BUILD_RC=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
fi
_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build

# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
_prep sigint
export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
#
# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
# operator to find which.
#
# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
# own timeout_s.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal

# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
_arm_release() {
    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
    # before the dispatch worked at all.
    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
    ${1:-:}
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    return 0
}
PLUG
}

# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
# hold on an idle machine.
#
# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
_arm_outcome() {
    local _o=pass
    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    ${1:-:}
    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
    return ${2:-0}
}
PLUG
}

# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
_run_case() {
    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    set +e
    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
    _CASE_RC=$?
    set -e
    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
}

# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
_run_case "rc0" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
_run_case "rc1" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
_arm_release
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
_run_case "rc130" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
_runner_pid=$!
# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
#
# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done
if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
fi
_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done

# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
#
# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
#
# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
# instead of starting another hunt.
if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    {
        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
    } >&2
fi
# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
fi
# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable always-run role is LOUD ───────────────
# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
# missing effect.
print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"
_arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER"
rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-unresolved"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
_unres_rc=$?
set -e
assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
# verdict, including when it could not be found.
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"

print_test_results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: _orch_local_kill_slot and the always-run watchdog in runner.sh kill
# through zbuild_pg_kill, not through direct `kill` (#1801, SPEC-6).
#
# Direct `kill -TERM/-KILL $pid` only reaches the named process. A hook that
# forks a child which ignores TERM (as in SPEC-6b) keeps that child alive when
# the watchdog fires on just the leader. zbuild_pg_kill sends to the whole
# process group (TERM then KILL), so the child is caught.
#
# This is a static guard: it searches the source files for the patterns
# that must NOT be there (direct kill in _orch_local_kill_slot) and the
# patterns that MUST be there (zbuild_pg_kill call in both sites).
#
# The test must FAIL on current code (which uses direct kill in both places)
# and PASS after the implementation switches to zbuild_pg_kill.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-6]
set -uo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch kill sites use zbuild_pg_kill (not direct kill) (#1801 SPEC-6)"
setup_test_env "orch-kill-uses-pg-kill-guard"

LOCAL_ENGINE="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

assert_file_exists "SPEC-0a: local_engine.sh exists" "$LOCAL_ENGINE"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0b: runner.sh exists" "$RUNNER"

# ── SPEC-6a: _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill ─────────────────────
# Extract the body of _orch_local_kill_slot (from its header to the closing }).
# After the fix it should call zbuild_pg_kill; on old code it calls direct kill.
_kill_slot_body="$(sed -n '/_orch_local_kill_slot\(\)/,/^}/p' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
        "body uses direct kill; after #1801 it must call zbuild_pg_kill for process-group coverage"
fi

# Old pattern: `kill -TERM/-KILL "$wrapper_pid"` individually (not zbuild_pg_kill).
# This must NOT appear in _orch_local_kill_slot after the fix.
if grep -qE 'kill\s+-TERM\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body" || \
   grep -qE 'kill\s+-KILL\s+"?\$wrapper_pid"?' <<< "$_kill_slot_body"; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid" \
        "still uses direct \`kill -TERM/-KILL \$wrapper_pid\`; must use zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _orch_local_kill_slot does not use bare kill on wrapper_pid"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b: always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
# The always-run watchdog is inside _runner_dispatch_always_run. Extract its
# subshell block (from `_runner_dispatch_always_run` to the closing `done`).
_ar_body="$(sed -n '/_runner_dispatch_always_run()/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    # fallback: grab from the function definition keyword to its end
    _ar_body="$(sed -n '/^    _runner_dispatch_always_run() {/,/^    }$/p' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] always-run watchdog in runner.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
        "_runner_dispatch_always_run uses direct kill; after #1801 the watchdog must call zbuild_pg_kill"
fi

# ── SPEC-6c: zbuild_pg_kill is defined and sourced by both files ─────────────
PG_KILL_LIB="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-6c: proc-group.sh defines zbuild_pg_kill" "$PG_KILL_LIB"
if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill()' "$PG_KILL_LIB" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] zbuild_pg_kill is defined in proc-group.sh" \
        "function not found in $PG_KILL_LIB"
fi
if grep -q 'proc-group' "$LOCAL_ENGINE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh (or its parent does)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] local_engine.sh sources proc-group.sh" \
        "no reference to proc-group.sh found in local_engine.sh"
fi

# ── SPEC-6 runtime: TERM-ignoring child leaves no running process ─────────────
# Behavioral guarantee: after the watchdog kills a slot whose wrapper spawned a
# child that ignores TERM, that child must also be gone.
#
# Old _orch_local_kill_slot: `kill "-${sig}" "$wrapper_pid"` only. Killing the
# wrapper with SIGKILL does not kill its children — they are orphaned and continue
# running. So a TERM-ignoring child outlives the watchdog on old code.
# New _orch_local_kill_slot: calls zbuild_pg_kill, which sends TERM then KILL to
# the WHOLE process group. The TERM-ignoring child receives KILL and exits.
#
# Fails on old code (child alive after collect kills wrapper).
# Passes on new code (process-group KILL reaches child).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child leaves no process after watchdog fires (runtime)"
# Source the implementations so the runtime paths execute (not just pattern-match).
# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/local_engine.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/proc-group.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"

_s6rt_pool="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-rt-pool"
mkdir -p "$_s6rt_pool/pids" "$_s6rt_pool/results"
_s6rt_child_file="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec6-rt-child.pid"

# Start the wrapper as a NEW process group (set -m → background job is group leader).
# The wrapper forks a child that ignores TERM and records its PID. The wrapper
# itself waits and never writes a .exit file, so _orch_local_collect_results will
# time out and call _orch_local_kill_slot to kill the slot.
set -m
(
    ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "$_s6rt_child_file"; sleep 120 ) &
    _s6rt_inner=$!
    trap ':' TERM
    wait "$_s6rt_inner" 2>/dev/null || true
) &
_s6rt_wrapper_pid=$!
set +m

printf '%s\n' "$_s6rt_wrapper_pid" > "$_s6rt_pool/pids/spec6rt.pid"
# No .inner_pid file: _orch_local_kill_slot only receives wrapper_pid, so the
# child can be reached only via process-group kill (the new code path).

# Wait for the child pid to be recorded (up to 5 s).
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do [[ -s "$_s6rt_child_file" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
_s6rt_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$_s6rt_child_file" 2>/dev/null || true)"

# Collect with 2 s timeout. The wrapper never writes .exit, so collect fires the
# kill path. After collect returns, the child should be dead (new code) or alive (old).
_s6rt_rc=0
_orch_local_collect_results "$_s6rt_pool" "pids" 2 || _s6rt_rc=$?

# Poll briefly: the KILL signal needs a moment to be processed.
_s6rt_alive=1
if [[ -n "$_s6rt_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
        kill -0 "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _s6rt_alive=0; break; }
        sleep 0.1
    done
fi

if [[ -z "$_s6rt_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] fixture: TERM-ignoring child recorded its pid" \
        "no pid written to $_s6rt_child_file (wrapper may not have started)"
elif [[ "$_s6rt_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child must not outlive the watchdog" \
        "pid $_s6rt_child_pid still alive; old code: direct kill misses TERM-ignoring children; new code: zbuild_pg_kill kills the group"
    kill -KILL "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_s6rt_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] TERM-ignoring child does not outlive the watchdog (group kill via zbuild_pg_kill)"
fi

print_test_results
