16	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
17	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
18	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
19	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
20	#
21	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
22	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
23	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
24	# mechanical gates; the objective-gate plugin was then removed in B7 (#1139).
25	# #2368: the engine combines the gates by build_test_cycle's exit_when, which
26	# names every member that must pass; gate-aggregator is retired.
27	#
28	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
29	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
30	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
31	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
32	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
33	# one work unit per lens element. #2368: the engine sums the lenses up
34	# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged
35	# (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED); review-aggregator is retired. The lens group is
36	# ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
37	# exit_when/convergence (build_test_cycle's exit_when, ADR-040 §5) and never
38	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
39	flow:
40	  - hydrate
41	  - intake
42	  - plan
43	  - delivery_loop
44	  - review_lenses
45	  - pr
46	
47	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
48	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
49	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
50	#
51	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
52	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
53	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
54	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
55	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
56	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
57	# called.
58	#
59	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
60	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
61	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
62	#
63	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
64	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
65	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
66	# quietly running nothing.
67	always_run:
68	  - release
69	  - persist
70	
71	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
72	# One outer loop holds design and the build loop. Every stage sees every
73	# finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine never
74	# decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
75	#   - design makes one model call per run and checks the design it wrote. One
76	#     that fails is `unusable`: the engine runs design again (its retry:), and
77	#     each run starts from the last good design and the last try's failures
78	#     (ADR-068 §8). A design that still fails ends the run — stop_run_on_fail:
79	#     build never runs on it, and another round would only repeat those tries.
80	delivery_loop:
81	  type: cycle
82	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
83	  flow:
84	    - design
85	    - build_test_cycle
86	  exit_when:
87	    all:
88	      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
89	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
90	  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
91	  max_iterations: 2
92	  on_max: halt
93	
94	# ─── test-author (leaf, build_test_cycle member; the loop requires it) ───────
95	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
96	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
97	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
98	test-author:
99	  gate: auto
100	  roles: [test_author]
101	  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (4 model calls of 15 minutes, plus a few minutes); the engine
102	  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
103	  timeout_s: 3780
104	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
105	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
106	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
107	  blocking: true
108	  router:
109	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
110	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
111	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
112	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
113	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
114	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
115	    timeout_s: 900
116	    max_turns: 0
117	    max_iterations: 4
118	
119	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
120	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
121	# path is allowed for the same reason as design's coverage check (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
122	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
123	issue-acceptance:
124	  gate: auto
125	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
126	  # Same question design's coverage check asks of the design — "was what was asked for
127	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
128	  persona: product-owner
129	  router:
130	    timeout_s: 600
131	
132	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
133	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
134	# mechanical gates. #2368: the engine combines them — exit_when names every
135	# member that must pass this round; one with no outcome this round counts as
136	# failed (the ADR-019 fail-closed contract). gate-aggregator is retired.
137	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
138	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
139	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
140	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
141	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
142	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
143	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
144	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
145	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
146	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
147	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
148	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
149	# which goes round from design.
150	build_test_cycle:
151	  type: cycle
152	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until every one passes
153	  flow:
154	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
155	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
156	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
157	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff. #2370: it then checks each
158	    # assertion tests what its SPEC says (was spec-correspondence), and the loop
159	    # requires it to pass — the SPEC is design's, which it cannot re-author.
160	    - test-author
161	    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
162	    - build
163	    - test
164	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
165	    # only check after design's own coverage check that reads the issue; each unmet
166	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
167	    - issue-acceptance
168	  exit_when:
169	    all:
170	      - { stage: test-author, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
171	      # #2371: build must pass — it scans its own change for secrets, and a
172	      # build that broke scope or did not finish is not done either.
173	      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
174	      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
175	      - { stage: issue-acceptance, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
176	  max_iterations: 3
177	  on_max: continue
178	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
179	intake:
180	  gate: auto
181	  roles: [intake]
182	  io:
183	    destinations: [file, stdout]
184	    tail_lines: 200
185	
186	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
187	plan:
188	  gate: auto
189	  roles: [planner]
190	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
191	  persona: product-owner
192	  io:
193	    destinations: [file, stdout]
194	    tail_lines: 200
195	  router:
196	    timeout_s: 300
197	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
198	    # headroom. The planner is
199	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
200	    max_turns: 45
201	
202	# ─── design (leaf, delivery_loop member) ───────────────────────────────
203	design:
204	  gate: auto
205	  roles: [designer]
206	  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (one 20-minute design call
207	  # and a 20-minute coverage call, plus a few minutes); the engine stops it
208	  # here. Each run is a new stage, with its own limit. The default is 900.
209	  timeout_s: 2700
210	  # ADR-068 §8: a run whose design cannot be used is run again, handed its
211	  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
212	  retry: 2
213	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
214	  persona: architect
215	  io:
216	    destinations: [file, stdout]
217	    tail_lines: 200
218	  router:
219	    # #1944: three 600s calls in a row ran out of time on a resumed run.
220	    timeout_s: 1200
221	    max_turns: 0
222	
223	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
224	build:
225	  gate: auto
226	  roles: [builder]
227	  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (3 rounds of 15-minute model calls, and more); the engine
228	  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
229	  timeout_s: 3600
230	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
231	  persona: developer
232	  io:
233	    destinations: [file, stdout]
234	    tail_lines: 200
235	  router:
236	    timeout_s: 900
237	    max_turns: 0
238	
239	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
240	test:
241	  gate: auto
242	  roles: [tester]
243	  # #2372: test runs the shape floor and the acceptance check over its own run,
244	  # and checks the assertion files against their fingerprints. ADR-036 #1188:
245	  # negctl_timeout_s bounds each requirement's negative-control / reachability
246	  # run (seconds).
247	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
248	  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (the full test suite); the engine
249	  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
250	  timeout_s: 2700
251	  io:
252	    destinations: [file, stdout]
253	    tail_lines: 200
254	
255	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
256	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
257	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
258	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
259	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
260	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
261	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
262	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
263	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
264	#
265	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
266	# Convergence is owned by build_test_cycle's exit_when above;
267	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
268	review_lenses:
269	  type: map
270	  # #2368: a lens fails on a problem the change introduced of these severities.
271	  fail_on: [high, critical]
272	  over: lenses
273	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
274	  # from the lens's name.
275	  elements:
276	    - id: security
277	      persona: security
278	    - id: performance
279	      persona: performance
280	    - id: red-team
281	      persona: red-team
282	    - id: correctness
283	      persona: correctness
284	    - id: scope
285	      persona: scope
286	    - id: sre
287	      persona: sre
288	  roles: [review_lens]
289	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
290	  max_parallel: 4
291	  on_member_error: continue
292	  aggregate: advisory
293	  io:
294	    destinations: [file]
295	    tail_lines: 200
296	  router:
297	    timeout_s: 300
298	    max_turns: 25
299	
300	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
301	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
302	pr:
303	  gate: auto
304	  roles: [pr]
305	  io:
306	    destinations: [file, stdout]
307	    tail_lines: 200
308	
309	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
310	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
311	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
312	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
313	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
314	#
315	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
316	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
317	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
318	release:
319	  gate: auto
320	  roles: [teardown]
321	  timeout_s: 30
322	  router:
323	    timeout_s: 30
324	  io:
325	    destinations: [file]
326	    tail_lines: 50
327	
328	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
329	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
330	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
331	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
332	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
333	# abort.
334	#
335	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
336	# process-group kill does not.
337	persist:
338	  gate: auto
339	  roles: [persist]
340	  timeout_s: 120
341	  router:
342	    timeout_s: 120
343	  io:
344	    destinations: [file]
345	    tail_lines: 50
346	
347	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
348	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
349	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
350	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
351	#
352	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
353	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
354	# an earlier push never delivered.
355	hydrate:
356	  gate: auto
357	  roles: [hydrate]
358	  # #2366: restoring less than all earlier work is reported as fail; the run
359	  # carries on without it rather than stopping.
360	  blocking: false
361	  router:
362	    timeout_s: 60
363	  io:
364	    destinations: [file]
365	    tail_lines: 50
366

file.content:
id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

# #2367: the run's branch; {key} is the run's identity (issue-<n>). A repository
# overrides it in .zbuild/branch; ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH overrides both.
branch: zbuild/{key}

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates; the objective-gate plugin was then removed in B7 (#1139).
# #2368: the engine combines the gates by build_test_cycle's exit_when, which
# names every member that must pass; gate-aggregator is retired.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element. #2368: the engine sums the lenses up
# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged
# (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED); review-aggregator is retired. The lens group is
# ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (build_test_cycle's exit_when, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds design and the build loop. Every stage sees every
# finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine never
# decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - design makes one model call per run and checks the design it wrote. One
#     that fails is `unusable`: the engine runs design again (its retry:), and
#     each run starts from the last good design and the last try's failures
#     (ADR-068 §8). A design that still fails ends the run — stop_run_on_fail:
#     build never runs on it, and another round would only repeat those tries.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── test-author (leaf, build_test_cycle member; the loop requires it) ───────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (4 model calls of 15 minutes, plus a few minutes); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3780
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as design's coverage check (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question design's coverage check asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates. #2368: the engine combines them — exit_when names every
# member that must pass this round; one with no outcome this round counts as
# failed (the ADR-019 fail-closed contract). gate-aggregator is retired.
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until every one passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff. #2370: it then checks each
    # assertion tests what its SPEC says (was spec-correspondence), and the loop
    # requires it to pass — the SPEC is design's, which it cannot re-author.
    - test-author
    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
    - build
    - test
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after design's own coverage check that reads the issue; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: test-author, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      # #2371: build must pass — it scans its own change for secrets, and a
      # build that broke scope or did not finish is not done either.
      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: issue-acceptance, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
    # headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, delivery_loop member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (one 20-minute design call
  # and a 20-minute coverage call, plus a few minutes); the engine stops it
  # here. Each run is a new stage, with its own limit. The default is 900.
  timeout_s: 2700
  # ADR-068 §8: a run whose design cannot be used is run again, handed its
  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
  retry: 2
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    # #1944: three 600s calls in a row ran out of time on a resumed run.
    timeout_s: 1200
    max_turns: 0

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (3 rounds of 15-minute model calls, and more); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3600
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  # #2372: test runs the shape floor and the acceptance check over its own run,
  # and checks the assertion files against their fingerprints. ADR-036 #1188:
  # negctl_timeout_s bounds each requirement's negative-control / reachability
  # run (seconds).
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (the full test suite); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 2700
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by build_test_cycle's exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  # #2368: a lens fails on a problem the change introduced of these severities.
  fail_on: [high, critical]
  over: lenses
  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  timeout_s: 30
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  timeout_s: 120
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
#
# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
# an earlier push never delivered.
hydrate:
  gate: auto
  roles: [hydrate]
  # #2366: restoring less than all earlier work is reported as fail; the run
  # carries on without it rather than stopping.
  blocking: false
  router:
    timeout_s: 60
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

1	# ADR-011: Pluggable Backends (Memory, Orchestrator, Cache)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Amended:** 2026-08-22 — retention: the cache store is reclaimable, the memory store never is
5	**Date:** 2026-05-24
6	
7	> **Memory split:** The "memory backend" in this ADR is **learning memory** —
8	> patterns extracted from past runs, vector embeddings of source code,
9	> architectural decisions, skill-success scores. It accumulates over time and
10	> spans pipelines.
11	>
12	> It is **NOT** pipeline-resume memory (which is defined by
13	> [ADR-006](ADR-006-resume-contract.md) and transported by
14	> [ADR-010](ADR-010-ci-cli-parity.md) cache backends). Resume state is
15	> operational ("continue at stage X iteration Y"); learning memory is
16	> educational ("similar issues in the past took 3 cycles to converge").
17	>
18	> The two memory models share no storage and have independent failure modes:
19	> learning memory can be totally unavailable and pipelines still resume
20	> correctly; resume memory can be wiped and pipelines still benefit from
21	> learned patterns on the next fresh run.
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	Three cross-cutting capabilities can be implemented multiple ways, and zBuild should not pick one implementation in core:
26	
27	1. **Memory backend** — where learned patterns, embeddings, and decisions live. Could be local SQLite, ruflo's HNSW vector store via MCP, a future cloud KV, etc.
28	2. **Orchestrator backend** — how parallel agents are spawned and coordinated. Could be plain bash subshells, ruflo's hive-mind, a future job-queue worker pool, etc.
29	3. **Cache backend** — where durable state persists across CI runs (covered in ADR-010); same pattern.
30	
31	User requirement: "I want the option to use ruflo memory and ruflo swarming/hive abilities — those are not hard dependencies early on but they need to be able to do it in the future, so the architecture needs to be set to handle that."
32	
33	Translation: ship working defaults that need zero external services; let ruflo (or anything else) drop in via the plugin contract.
34	
35	## Decision
36	
37	Each capability gets a **backend contract** (a fixed set of function names + I/O shapes). A "backend" is just a plugin (`kind: tool`, with `provides.role: memory-backend` etc.) that implements the contract. zBuild ships defaults; users select alternates via `.zbuild/config.yaml`.
38	
39	### Memory backend contract
40	
41	```bash
42	memory_put <namespace> <key> <value>                 # store
43	memory_get <namespace> <key>                          # → value or empty
44	memory_search <namespace> <query> [--limit N]         # → list of matches
45	memory_list_namespaces                                # → list of strings
46	memory_namespace_exists <namespace>                   # exit 0/1
47	memory_namespace_clear <namespace>                    # destructive cleanup
48	```
49	
50	Optional (backends MAY implement; callers MUST handle absence):
51	```bash
52	memory_search_vector <namespace> <embedding>          # vector similarity search
53	memory_capabilities                                   # → JSON of declared capabilities
54	```
55	
56	**Default implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/` — local SQLite at `~/.zbuild/state/memory.db`, TF-IDF text search via `LIKE %query%`, no vector support. Always works, no external deps.
57	
58	**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/` — proxies to ruflo MCP for HNSW vector search. Requires `ruflo` binary on PATH; `memory_capabilities` declares `["vector_search", "hnsw"]`.
59	
60	### Orchestrator backend contract
61	
62	```bash
63	orch_spawn <pool_id> <count> <role_arg>               # spawn N workers
64	orch_dispatch <pool_id> <task_json>                   # send work to pool
65	orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]                  # gather results; exit 0=all pass, 1=all fail, 2=partial
66	orch_shutdown <pool_id>                               # cleanup
67	orch_capabilities                                     # → JSON
68	```
69	
70	**(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now `orch_collect` returns 0 (all passed) or 1, naming mixed results on `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
71	
72	**`orch_collect` exit code convention (all implementations must honour this):**
73	- `0` — all dispatched work units exited 0 (success); pool dir removed.
74	- `1` — all dispatched work units exited non-zero (complete failure).
75	- `2` — mixed results: at least one unit passed and at least one failed (partial). **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**
76	
77	Work-unit exit codes are normalised — individual codes are not passed through. Strategies use `2` to emit `stage.fail reason=partial` via the runner. **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=partial`)**
78	
79	**Phase 0.5 default implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` — single-process, in-order dispatch. Chosen as the default for Phase 0.5 because it has zero coordination surface and the smallest reference impl of the 0/1/2 normalisation contract. The `.zbuild/config.yaml` snippet below shows how to opt in to one of the optional backends.
80	
81	**Parallel implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/` — uses bash subshells + `wait -n` for parallelism, no coordination beyond independent execution. Implements `fanout` and `sequential` strategies trivially; `composite` works via a single subshell.
82	
83	**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/` — proxies to `ruflo hive-mind init/spawn/orchestrate`. Implements all three strategies natively; provides queen-collapse synthesis and shared-memory namespacing. `orch_capabilities` declares `["hive_mind", "queen_collapse", "shared_memory"]`.
84	
85	### Cache backend contract (covered in ADR-010)
86	
87	```bash
88	cache_pull <key> <dest_dir>                           # restore from cache key into dest_dir
89	cache_push <key> <src_dir>                            # snapshot src_dir under cache key
90	cache_capabilities                                    # → JSON
91	```
92	
93	The `<key>` is an opaque, plugin-agnostic identifier (e.g., a slot id or a content hash). The `<dest_dir>` / `<src_dir>` makes the caller's intent explicit and lets a single cache backend serve multiple consumers (resume snapshot, build artifact, etc.) within one run.
94	
95	Reconciled with the code (`core/cache/contract.sh`) on 2026-05-26 per #310: the initial sketch used a single-arg `cache_pull <slot_id>` that conflated key and destination. The two-arg form is what every implementation already needs and what the existing `gh-actions-cache` / `cache-local` plugins ship.
96	
97	Defaults: `local` — a real filesystem-backed cache under `$ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR` (defaults to `~/.zbuild/cache`). Optionals: `gh-actions-cache`, `s3`, `gist`.
98	
99	### Backend selection: `.zbuild/config.yaml`
100	
101	> **Scope note:** backend pluggability covers **memory, orchestrator, and cache only**. Model routing is core per ADR-003 — `core/router/route.sh` is not a backend and is not selectable via this config.
102	
103	```yaml
104	backends:
105	  memory: sqlite                    # default; or "ruflo"
106	  orchestrator: sequential          # default; or "bash-parallel", "ruflo-hive"
107	  cache: local                      # default; or "gh-actions-cache", "s3"
108	
109	# Optional per-backend config
110	memory_ruflo:
111	  mcp_server: "ruflo"
112	  namespace_prefix: "zbuild"
113	  fallback_to_default_on_error: true
114	
115	orchestrator_ruflo:
116	  topology: hierarchical
117	  max_agents: 8
118	  hive_timeout_sec: 300
119	```
120	
121	Resolution at startup: read config, look up the named backend in the plugin registry, verify it implements the contract. If a backend is selected but missing, `zbuild doctor` flags it. **Critical**: when a non-default backend is selected, callers MUST handle `_capabilities` differences (e.g., don't request `memory_search_vector` from the SQLite default).
122	
123	### Graceful degradation rules
124	
125	1. **Default backend always works.** Out-of-box experience requires nothing more than `./install.sh` (per ADR-023).
126	2. **Optional backend can be configured but unavailable at runtime** (e.g., ruflo daemon crashed). Each backend declares `fallback_to_default_on_error: true|false`. If true, runtime falls back to default with a `backend.degraded` event; if false, hard-fails with a clear error.
127	3. **Backend capabilities are declarative.** Callers query `<backend>_capabilities` and choose a code path based on what's available. Example: pipeline-intelligence might do vector search if `vector_search` is in capabilities, TF-IDF otherwise.
128	
129	### Plugin manifest extension
130	
131	Memory and orchestrator backends are `kind: tool` plugins with a special `provides.role`:
132	
133	```yaml
134	# plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/manifest.yaml
135	id: memory-sqlite
136	kind: tool
137	provides:
138	  role: memory-backend                  # marks as backend implementation
139	  capabilities: [text_search, namespacing, persistence]
140	
141	# plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/manifest.yaml
142	id: memory-ruflo
143	kind: tool
144	provides:
145	  role: memory-backend
146	  capabilities: [text_search, vector_search, hnsw, namespacing, persistence, distributed]
147	requires:
148	  bin: [ruflo]                          # NEW manifest field: required binaries
149	```
150	
151	The plugin registry can list all backends of a role: `zbuild plugin list --role memory-backend`.
152	
153	## Consequences
154	
155	**Good:**
156	- Zero external dependencies for the out-of-box experience.
157	- Adding a new backend (e.g., Pinecone, Redis, Dragonfly) = drop a plugin, declare capabilities, done.
158	- Tests for the engine never need ruflo running.
159	- Users opt in to advanced features (HNSW, hive-mind) by config, not by code change.
160	- Failure modes are explicit: missing backend → doctor warns; runtime backend crash → graceful fallback if configured.
161	
162	**Bad:**
163	- More plugins to maintain (defaults + ruflo + future variants).
164	- Callers must check `_capabilities` before using optional features; easy to forget.
165	- Backend selection lives in config; users with broken configs may not realize a feature is silently using the default.
166	
167	**Open questions:**
168	- Should backends be per-namespace? (e.g., "use SQLite for cost ledger, ruflo HNSW for embeddings"). Initial design: per-capability is the unit (memory backend is one choice; can't split). Revisit if real demand.
169	- Should `_capabilities` results be cached or queried every run? Initial: queried once at backend init.
170	
171	## Retention (amended 2026-08-22)
172	
173	This ADR defined two stores that outlive a run and said nothing about ever

# ADR-011: Pluggable Backends (Memory, Orchestrator, Cache)

**Status:** Accepted
**Amended:** 2026-08-22 — retention: the cache store is reclaimable, the memory store never is
**Date:** 2026-05-24

> **Memory split:** The "memory backend" in this ADR is **learning memory** —
> patterns extracted from past runs, vector embeddings of source code,
> architectural decisions, skill-success scores. It accumulates over time and
> spans pipelines.
>
> It is **NOT** pipeline-resume memory (which is defined by
> [ADR-006](ADR-006-resume-contract.md) and transported by
> [ADR-010](ADR-010-ci-cli-parity.md) cache backends). Resume state is
> operational ("continue at stage X iteration Y"); learning memory is
> educational ("similar issues in the past took 3 cycles to converge").
>
> The two memory models share no storage and have independent failure modes:
> learning memory can be totally unavailable and pipelines still resume
> correctly; resume memory can be wiped and pipelines still benefit from
> learned patterns on the next fresh run.

## Context

Three cross-cutting capabilities can be implemented multiple ways, and zBuild should not pick one implementation in core:

1. **Memory backend** — where learned patterns, embeddings, and decisions live. Could be local SQLite, ruflo's HNSW vector store via MCP, a future cloud KV, etc.
2. **Orchestrator backend** — how parallel agents are spawned and coordinated. Could be plain bash subshells, ruflo's hive-mind, a future job-queue worker pool, etc.
3. **Cache backend** — where durable state persists across CI runs (covered in ADR-010); same pattern.

User requirement: "I want the option to use ruflo memory and ruflo swarming/hive abilities — those are not hard dependencies early on but they need to be able to do it in the future, so the architecture needs to be set to handle that."

Translation: ship working defaults that need zero external services; let ruflo (or anything else) drop in via the plugin contract.

## Decision

Each capability gets a **backend contract** (a fixed set of function names + I/O shapes). A "backend" is just a plugin (`kind: tool`, with `provides.role: memory-backend` etc.) that implements the contract. zBuild ships defaults; users select alternates via `.zbuild/config.yaml`.

### Memory backend contract

```bash
memory_put <namespace> <key> <value>                 # store
memory_get <namespace> <key>                          # → value or empty
memory_search <namespace> <query> [--limit N]         # → list of matches
memory_list_namespaces                                # → list of strings
memory_namespace_exists <namespace>                   # exit 0/1
memory_namespace_clear <namespace>                    # destructive cleanup
```

Optional (backends MAY implement; callers MUST handle absence):
```bash
memory_search_vector <namespace> <embedding>          # vector similarity search
memory_capabilities                                   # → JSON of declared capabilities
```

**Default implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/` — local SQLite at `~/.zbuild/state/memory.db`, TF-IDF text search via `LIKE %query%`, no vector support. Always works, no external deps.

**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/` — proxies to ruflo MCP for HNSW vector search. Requires `ruflo` binary on PATH; `memory_capabilities` declares `["vector_search", "hnsw"]`.

### Orchestrator backend contract

```bash
orch_spawn <pool_id> <count> <role_arg>               # spawn N workers
orch_dispatch <pool_id> <task_json>                   # send work to pool
orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]                  # gather results; exit 0=all pass, 1=all fail, 2=partial
orch_shutdown <pool_id>                               # cleanup
orch_capabilities                                     # → JSON
```

**(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now `orch_collect` returns 0 (all passed) or 1, naming mixed results on `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**

**`orch_collect` exit code convention (all implementations must honour this):**
- `0` — all dispatched work units exited 0 (success); pool dir removed.
- `1` — all dispatched work units exited non-zero (complete failure).
- `2` — mixed results: at least one unit passed and at least one failed (partial). **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=partial`)**

Work-unit exit codes are normalised — individual codes are not passed through. Strategies use `2` to emit `stage.fail reason=partial` via the runner. **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME=partial`)**

**Phase 0.5 default implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` — single-process, in-order dispatch. Chosen as the default for Phase 0.5 because it has zero coordination surface and the smallest reference impl of the 0/1/2 normalisation contract. The `.zbuild/config.yaml` snippet below shows how to opt in to one of the optional backends.

**Parallel implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/` — uses bash subshells + `wait -n` for parallelism, no coordination beyond independent execution. Implements `fanout` and `sequential` strategies trivially; `composite` works via a single subshell.

**Optional implementation**: `plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/` — proxies to `ruflo hive-mind init/spawn/orchestrate`. Implements all three strategies natively; provides queen-collapse synthesis and shared-memory namespacing. `orch_capabilities` declares `["hive_mind", "queen_collapse", "shared_memory"]`.

### Cache backend contract (covered in ADR-010)

```bash
cache_pull <key> <dest_dir>                           # restore from cache key into dest_dir
cache_push <key> <src_dir>                            # snapshot src_dir under cache key
cache_capabilities                                    # → JSON
```

The `<key>` is an opaque, plugin-agnostic identifier (e.g., a slot id or a content hash). The `<dest_dir>` / `<src_dir>` makes the caller's intent explicit and lets a single cache backend serve multiple consumers (resume snapshot, build artifact, etc.) within one run.

Reconciled with the code (`core/cache/contract.sh`) on 2026-05-26 per #310: the initial sketch used a single-arg `cache_pull <slot_id>` that conflated key and destination. The two-arg form is what every implementation already needs and what the existing `gh-actions-cache` / `cache-local` plugins ship.

Defaults: `local` — a real filesystem-backed cache under `$ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR` (defaults to `~/.zbuild/cache`). Optionals: `gh-actions-cache`, `s3`, `gist`.

### Backend selection: `.zbuild/config.yaml`

> **Scope note:** backend pluggability covers **memory, orchestrator, and cache only**. Model routing is core per ADR-003 — `core/router/route.sh` is not a backend and is not selectable via this config.

```yaml
backends:
  memory: sqlite                    # default; or "ruflo"
  orchestrator: sequential          # default; or "bash-parallel", "ruflo-hive"
  cache: local                      # default; or "gh-actions-cache", "s3"

# Optional per-backend config
memory_ruflo:
  mcp_server: "ruflo"
  namespace_prefix: "zbuild"
  fallback_to_default_on_error: true

orchestrator_ruflo:
  topology: hierarchical
  max_agents: 8
  hive_timeout_sec: 300
```

Resolution at startup: read config, look up the named backend in the plugin registry, verify it implements the contract. If a backend is selected but missing, `zbuild doctor` flags it. **Critical**: when a non-default backend is selected, callers MUST handle `_capabilities` differences (e.g., don't request `memory_search_vector` from the SQLite default).

### Graceful degradation rules

1. **Default backend always works.** Out-of-box experience requires nothing more than `./install.sh` (per ADR-023).
2. **Optional backend can be configured but unavailable at runtime** (e.g., ruflo daemon crashed). Each backend declares `fallback_to_default_on_error: true|false`. If true, runtime falls back to default with a `backend.degraded` event; if false, hard-fails with a clear error.
3. **Backend capabilities are declarative.** Callers query `<backend>_capabilities` and choose a code path based on what's available. Example: pipeline-intelligence might do vector search if `vector_search` is in capabilities, TF-IDF otherwise.

### Plugin manifest extension

Memory and orchestrator backends are `kind: tool` plugins with a special `provides.role`:

```yaml
# plugins/tool/memory-sqlite/manifest.yaml
id: memory-sqlite
kind: tool
provides:
  role: memory-backend                  # marks as backend implementation
  capabilities: [text_search, namespacing, persistence]

# plugins/tool/memory-ruflo/manifest.yaml
id: memory-ruflo
kind: tool
provides:
  role: memory-backend
  capabilities: [text_search, vector_search, hnsw, namespacing, persistence, distributed]
requires:
  bin: [ruflo]                          # NEW manifest field: required binaries
```

The plugin registry can list all backends of a role: `zbuild plugin list --role memory-backend`.

## Consequences

**Good:**
- Zero external dependencies for the out-of-box experience.
- Adding a new backend (e.g., Pinecone, Redis, Dragonfly) = drop a plugin, declare capabilities, done.
- Tests for the engine never need ruflo running.
- Users opt in to advanced features (HNSW, hive-mind) by config, not by code change.
- Failure modes are explicit: missing backend → doctor warns; runtime backend crash → graceful fallback if configured.

**Bad:**
- More plugins to maintain (defaults + ruflo + future variants).
- Callers must check `_capabilities` before using optional features; easy to forget.
- Backend selection lives in config; users with broken configs may not realize a feature is silently using the default.

**Open questions:**
- Should backends be per-namespace? (e.g., "use SQLite for cost ledger, ruflo HNSW for embeddings"). Initial design: per-capability is the unit (memory backend is one choice; can't split). Revisit if real demand.
- Should `_capabilities` results be cached or queried every run? Initial: queried once at backend init.

## Retention (amended 2026-08-22)

This ADR defined two stores that outlive a run and said nothing about ever
reclaiming either. They are not the same, and the difference is now a rule:

| Store | Default location | Reclaimed? |
|---|---|---|
| **Cache** | `${ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR:-~/.zbuild/cache}/<key>` | **Yes** — `zbuild cleanup --cache`, in the default set, aged from last touch |
| **Memory** | `~/.zbuild/state/memory.db` | **Never** |

**The cache is reclaimable because a miss is a normal outcome.** `cache_pull`
prints `CACHE_MISS` and returns 0 by contract, so deleting an entry costs a
recomputation and nothing else. It is content-addressed by key, not keyed to an
issue, so it ages from last touch like any other regenerable artifact.

**The memory store is never reclaimed, and this is a rule, not an omission.** It
is deliberately agnostic to the issues it supports — the knowledge it holds is
not the residue of any one run and does not expire when that run's artifacts do.
No cleanup target may name it, and `tests/unit/cleanup-new-reclaimers-test.sh`
SPEC-4 asserts that `scripts/lib/cleanup.sh` contains no reference to it. If a
future need to prune memory arises, it belongs behind its own deliberate command
with its own reasoning, not folded into artifact reclamation.

## Implementation Notes (Phase 0.5 — issue #291)

| Item | Status | PR / Notes |
|------|--------|------------|
| Cache backend contract (local file + GH Actions cache) | Implemented | #211 (issue #82); local default wired |
| Memory backend contract (local JSON + SQLite) | Implemented | #215, #216 (SQLite trial) |
| Memory-ruflo optional backend | Implemented | #217 (issue #215/217) |
| Orchestrator backend contract (sequential default) | Implemented | #219 (issue #88) |
| Orchestrator-ruflo hive-mind optional backend | Implemented | #221 (issue #89) |
| `_capabilities` query + graceful fallback | Implemented | all backend PRs above follow this pattern |
| Ruflo HNSW / Pinecone / Redis additional backends | Deferred → Phase 1 | KEEPERS.md §B1 wish list |

## Enforced by

- §Orchestrator backend contract (§ orch_load_backend must fail when backend is absent, not fall back silently) — `tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh` [#1801/SPEC-2], [#1801/SPEC-4], [#1801/SPEC-10].
- §No sequential fallback (§ the built-in orch-sequential fallback is removed from orch_load_backend) — `tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh` [#1801/SPEC-2] and `tests/unit/orch-sequential-absent-guard-test.sh` [#1801/SPEC-3].
- §orch-sequential plugin directory absent from the installed tree — `tests/unit/orch-sequential-absent-guard-test.sh` [#1801/SPEC-3].
- §Memory store is never reclaimed — `tests/unit/cleanup-new-reclaimers-test.sh` SPEC-4.

## References

- [ADR-001 — Plugin Contract](ADR-001-plugin-contract.md) — backends are plugins
- [ADR-010 — CI / CLI Parity](ADR-010-ci-cli-parity.md) — cache backends follow same pattern
- ruf-1..5 issues (#102-#106) — implement the ruflo memory backend as ONE of multiple options, not the only one
- db-1..6 issues (#125-#130) — implement the SQLite default memory backend's tables

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Guard: a test that force-kills a runner must not undercut the engine's own
3	# teardown budget (#2029).
4	#
5	# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-5 sends SIGTERM, then force-kills the
6	# runner after a grace period, then asserts every stage wrote its release line.
7	# The grace was a hardcoded `sleep 3`.
8	#
9	# The engine bounds each release hook at ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, default **30s**
10	# (`core/pipeline/runner.sh:2025`), PER STAGE. Three stages release in that case,
11	# so teardown is entitled to take far longer than three seconds. When it did, the
12	# test killed the very thing it was about to assert on, and the marker came back
13	# EMPTY — both stages missing, not one:
14	#
15	#     ✗ [SPEC-5] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: intake build
16	#       no release from: intake build | marker=
17	#
18	# Reproduced deterministically by shortening the grace to 0.2s: identical
19	# signature. That is the mechanism — not machine load, though load is what made
20	# teardown slow enough to hit it.
21	#
22	# The durable invariant is not a bigger number. It is that the grace must be
23	# DERIVED from the budget it is protecting, so the two cannot drift apart again.
24	set -uo pipefail
25	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
26	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
27	
28	print_test_header "exit-path tests do not undercut the engine's teardown budget (#2029)"
29	setup_test_env "exit-path-teardown-budget"
30	
31	T="$REPO_ROOT/tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh"
32	assert_file_exists "SPEC-0: the integration test exists" "$T"
33	
34	# ── SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins the engine's release budget ────────────
35	# Unpinned, it is the 30s default and the test is racing a number it does not
36	# control. Pinning makes teardown's worst case knowable.
37	# After #1801 the pin is _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (the template `timeout_s:` for the
38	# release stage), replacing ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT which the engine no longer reads.
39	_spec5_block="$(sed -n '/SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill/,/SPEC-6/p' "$T")"
40	if grep -q '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
41	    assert_pass "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (template timeout_s: for release)"
42	else
43	    assert_fail "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (template timeout_s: for release)" \
44	        "unpinned — teardown may take the 30s default per stage while the test force-kills far sooner"
45	fi
46	
47	# ── SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived, not a literal ─────────────────
48	# The bug in one line. A literal cannot track the budget it is meant to outlast,
49	# and this one was 10x too small.
50	if grep -qE '\(\s*sleep\s+[0-9.]+\s*;\s*kill\s+-KILL' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
51	    assert_fail "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget" \
52	        "hardcoded literal in \`( sleep N; kill -KILL ... )\` — cannot track the budget it protects"
53	else
54	    assert_pass "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget"
55	fi
56	
57	# ── SPEC-3: and the derivation actually clears the worst case ─────────────
58	# Derived is not sufficient if the arithmetic is wrong. Three stages release on
59	# this path, each bounded independently, so the grace must clear 3x the per-hook
60	# bound. Evaluated rather than pattern-matched: the grace is an expression, and a
61	# guard that only recognised a literal would pass the moment someone wrote one.
62	_pinned="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=[0-9]+' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
63	_expr="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\([^)]*\)\)' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | sed -E 's/^_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\((.*)\)\)$/\1/')"
64	_graceval=""
65	if [[ -n "$_pinned" && -n "$_expr" ]]; then
66	    # Only our own arithmetic reaches here, and only after the two greps above
67	    # matched the exact shapes; nothing external is evaluated.
68	    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT="$_pinned"
69	    _graceval="$(( _expr ))" 2>/dev/null || _graceval=""
70	fi
71	if [[ -n "$_graceval" ]] && (( _graceval >= _pinned * 3 )); then
72	    assert_pass "SPEC-3: grace ${_graceval}s clears 3 stages x ${_pinned}s"
73	else
74	    assert_fail "SPEC-3: grace clears 3 stages x the per-hook bound" \
75	        "pinned='${_pinned:-none}' grace='${_graceval:-unevaluatable}' — need grace >= 3x pinned"
76	fi
77	
78	print_test_results
79

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: a test that force-kills a runner must not undercut the engine's own
# teardown budget (#2029).
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-5 sends SIGTERM, then force-kills the
# runner after a grace period, then asserts every stage wrote its release line.
# The grace was a hardcoded `sleep 3`.
#
# The engine bounds each release hook at ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, default **30s**
# (`core/pipeline/runner.sh:2025`), PER STAGE. Three stages release in that case,
# so teardown is entitled to take far longer than three seconds. When it did, the
# test killed the very thing it was about to assert on, and the marker came back
# EMPTY — both stages missing, not one:
#
#     ✗ [SPEC-5] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: intake build
#       no release from: intake build | marker=
#
# Reproduced deterministically by shortening the grace to 0.2s: identical
# signature. That is the mechanism — not machine load, though load is what made
# teardown slow enough to hit it.
#
# The durable invariant is not a bigger number. It is that the grace must be
# DERIVED from the budget it is protecting, so the two cannot drift apart again.
set -uo pipefail
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "exit-path tests do not undercut the engine's teardown budget (#2029)"
setup_test_env "exit-path-teardown-budget"

T="$REPO_ROOT/tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0: the integration test exists" "$T"

# ── SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins the engine's release budget ────────────
# Unpinned, it is the 30s default and the test is racing a number it does not
# control. Pinning makes teardown's worst case knowable.
# After #1801 the pin is _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (the template `timeout_s:` for the
# release stage), replacing ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT which the engine no longer reads.
_spec5_block="$(sed -n '/SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill/,/SPEC-6/p' "$T")"
if grep -q '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
    assert_pass "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (template timeout_s: for release)"
else
    assert_fail "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT (template timeout_s: for release)" \
        "unpinned — teardown may take the 30s default per stage while the test force-kills far sooner"
fi

# ── SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived, not a literal ─────────────────
# The bug in one line. A literal cannot track the budget it is meant to outlast,
# and this one was 10x too small.
if grep -qE '\(\s*sleep\s+[0-9.]+\s*;\s*kill\s+-KILL' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
    assert_fail "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget" \
        "hardcoded literal in \`( sleep N; kill -KILL ... )\` — cannot track the budget it protects"
else
    assert_pass "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget"
fi

# ── SPEC-3: and the derivation actually clears the worst case ─────────────
# Derived is not sufficient if the arithmetic is wrong. Three stages release on
# this path, each bounded independently, so the grace must clear 3x the per-hook
# bound. Evaluated rather than pattern-matched: the grace is an expression, and a
# guard that only recognised a literal would pass the moment someone wrote one.
_pinned="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=[0-9]+' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
_expr="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\([^)]*\)\)' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | sed -E 's/^_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\((.*)\)\)$/\1/')"
_graceval=""
if [[ -n "$_pinned" && -n "$_expr" ]]; then
    # Only our own arithmetic reaches here, and only after the two greps above
    # matched the exact shapes; nothing external is evaluated.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT="$_pinned"
    _graceval="$(( _expr ))" 2>/dev/null || _graceval=""
fi
if [[ -n "$_graceval" ]] && (( _graceval >= _pinned * 3 )); then
    assert_pass "SPEC-3: grace ${_graceval}s clears 3 stages x ${_pinned}s"
else
    assert_fail "SPEC-3: grace clears 3 stages x the per-hook bound" \
        "pinned='${_pinned:-none}' grace='${_graceval:-unevaluatable}' — need grace >= 3x pinned"
fi

print_test_results
